title: Black Light FTL Physical-Topology to Family-Hazard Applicability Registry
purpose: Provides provenance-bearing canon links between ordinary gravitational/topological evidence and fictional family-specific hazards. It replaces caller-supplied boolean applicability with explicit family/named-technology records while preserving the rule that ordinary gravity cannot manufacture exotic FTL canon.

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Gravitational shear-plane/hyperlane methods are especially sensitive to underlying gravitational geometry; forks in a shear lane may catastrophically divide the transiting vessel; safety systems require predictive sensing and emergency de-transit with increasing but never perfect margins.

authorityOrder: caller simulation context only when explicitly marked non-canonical

NORMALIZED_TIDAL_DEGENERACY_BOUNDARY.definition: Operational boundary where gamma_ij = |lambda_i-lambda_j| / max(|lambda_i|,|lambda_j|,||T||_F,epsilon) reaches the versioned branch-identity threshold.
NORMALIZED_TIDAL_DEGENERACY_BOUNDARY.physicalStatus: DERIVED from ordinary weak-field tidal geometry and propagated measurement uncertainty
NORMALIZED_TIDAL_DEGENERACY_BOUNDARY.canonLimit: Evidence of changing/degenerate tidal topology, not itself evidence of an exotic lane, fork, wall, manifold defect, or transit boundary.

source.title: The different lightspeed methods
source.basis: The source explicitly describes transit along gravitational shear planes, extreme sensitivity to underlying gravitational conditions, and catastrophic destruction when a gravity-shear lane forks.

records.scope: The normalized tidal-degeneracy boundary may be used as a conservative physical precursor to a separately certified gravitational-plane shear-fork blocker. It may move an already-authorized blocker earlier but may not create a blocker when no family hazard has been certified.
machineryObligations: emergency de-transit or safe-plane shunt authority

source.title: The different lightspeed methods
source.basis: The source establishes gravity-sensitive shear transit generally, but does not by itself establish that every slipstream adhesion-loss event is a tidal branch fork. This record therefore remains supporting rather than blocker-authorizing.

records.scope: Tidal topology may inform slipstream/shear sensing, maintenance and route confidence for adhesion loss, but this generic relationship does not move a certified blocker earlier. A named technology source may strengthen or reject it.

resolutionRules: Named technology/vessel/installation records outrank family records within their documented scope.
Two equal-precedence contradictory records produce CONFLICT; the resolver must not guess.
No matching record produces UNRESOLVED, not NOT_APPLICABLE and not false.

APPLICABLE means the physical evidence may condition a separately certified fictional hazard; only REQUIRED_PHYSICAL_PRECURSOR authorizes conservative blocker tightening in the generic certification chain.
SUPPORTING_PHYSICAL_PRECURSOR preserves evidence for sensing/maintenance/confidence but does not move a blocker earlier without a stronger named authority.
NOT_APPLICABLE requires an explicit authority record; absence of a record is unresolved.
A simulation-only caller override may be returned only when canonicalResolutionRequired is false and must remain visibly SIMULATION_ONLY.
canonSafeguards: Ordinary tidal geometry cannot establish that any FTL family is physically real.
A physical normalized-degeneracy boundary is not automatically a shear fork, lane edge, slipstream wall, manifold defect, or blocker.
Applicability changes how already-authorized fictional hazards consume physical evidence; it does not authorize the fictional hazard itself.
Race/species identity does not imply family identity without a race/named technology source.
Missing applicability authority is UNRESOLVED rather than false, zero, or benign.
Operator, manufacturer, archaeological inference, and machinery ancestry must remain separate provenance fields when known.
